text:
Avery: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands panel  drop short Qs about mission, positioning, market focus, or competitive calls and we'll add answers.
Priya: For external comms, can we use the phrase "production economics"? marketing wants a 3-word headline.
Mateo: Yes to "production economics". It maps to cost/latency/reliability and is concise.
Zoe: How do we differentiate vs giant cloud providers in a single sentence for AE outreach?
Avery: Try: "Redwood offers predictable, low-latency inference with cost controls and enterprise-grade operational tooling." Keep it factual.
Carlos: Sales asks: when a prospect says "we already have endpoints with CloudX" what's the 2-line rebuttal?
Mateo: "CloudX endpoints are convenient; Redwood reduces per-token cost at scale and provides operational controls (dedicated pools, KV caching, rollouts) that make production predictable." Offer a joint benchmark.
Priya: Competitor list for RFPs? need 2-3 names to call out in a private response.
LegalBot: Approved comparatives for private RFPs: BigCloud (managed endpoints), ModelCo (self-host stacks), FastServe (inference runtimes). Use only verifiable metrics.
Zoe: Messaging nuance: should we ever say "we're better" in public slides?
Avery: Avoid superlatives without a citation. Instead use "X% lower latency in our benchmark suite (link)" when we have reproducible numbers.
Carlos: Roadmap clarity: can AEs say "improved batching and caching in Q3"?
Mateo: Public phrasing: "upcoming batching and caching optimizations (H2)". Specific quarters only under NDA.
Priya: One-liner for homepage? marketing asked for something under 12 words.
Avery: Use: "Predictable, economical LLM inference for engineering teams." Short and approved.
Zoe: Any change in target segments this quarter? are we shifting away from startups?
Avery: No pivot. Keep PLG-first for product-led growth; expand targeted enterprise plays for Dedicated/Private where appropriate.
Carlos: Quick ask: can leadership drop a copy-ready paragraph we can paste into AE outreach?
Avery: I'll post a 2-paragraph sales-ready blurb here later today. Tag me if you need it urgently.
Priya: Thanks! small note  prefer "cost-aware inference" in one-liners instead of "cheap".
Avery: Noted. We'll standardize language in the AE kit.
Mateo: Perf refs: use the sanitized numbers in the public AE branch of the perf repo: https://git.example.com/redwood/perf-suites/tree/public-ae-quick
LegalBot: Reminder: public claims must be supported by the referenced repo branch or the perf slide deck.
Avery: Great thread. Keep Qs short and we'll keep the answers concise. :rocket:
